To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hepatocellular c-Met and the systemic gp130 signalling are essential to control the innate immune response, the APR and the inflammatory response in the liver during cholestasis.
the hepatocyte-specific knockout of c-Met or gp130 leads to an impaired hepatic antibacterial response and a higher lethality after biliary obstruction.
gp130 and c-met are involved in controlling bacterial infection, the acute-phase reaction and the innate immune response, and thus in preventing sepsis and hepatic damage during cholestasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of innate immunity and the acute phase response by hepatocyte-specific c-Met/gP130 signalling in the liver.
the role of the hepatocyte-specific c-Met receptor and the interleukin-6 receptor in the innate immune response during cholestatic liver damage and the development of sepsis.
the regulation and function of hepatic innate immune responses in the context of cholestatic conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the c-Met and IL6/gp130 signalling pathways are involved in the control of hepatic innate immune response, the APR and thus in the protection against sepsis and cholestatic liver damage.

c-Met and IL6/gp130 are involved in the regulation of the innate immune system and that their loss leads to a higher rate of sepsis in cholestatic conditions, which is associated with a reduced antibacterial response and a higher rate of liver injury.
the hepatic expression of c-Met and IL6/gp130 is essential for a coordinated hepatic response during the onset of biliary cholestasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lack of c-Met and/or gp130 expression leads to a reduced hepatic antibacterial response and a higher lethality after BDL.
c-Met and IL6/gp130 cooperate to control the antibacterial response in the liver.

the lack of hepatic Gp130 and/or c-Met is associated with an increased bacterial load, an enhanced inflammatory response and a higher lethality in the acute phase of cholestatic conditions, which is caused by a defective antibacterial response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HGF/c-MET and IL-6/ gp130 are important for the hepatic innate immune response during cholestatic liver failure.
the lack of c-Met or gp130 expression in hepatocytes results in an impaired antibacterial and innate hepatic response, which is associated with an increased lethality after cholestatic liver insult.
the hepatic antibacteric and innate immune response are regulated by the HGF/c-MET and IL-6/IL-6 receptor signalling pathways, which are involved in the control of the acute phase response.
